items.title: LiteLLM v1.102.0 — guardrails finally run on streaming responses
items.summary: Post-call guardrails stop being an end-of-response check and start rewriting text while it streams.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.156.1 — GPT-6 Sol and Luna join the model picker
items.summary: One day after OpenAI launched them, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are selectable inside the Codex CLI.

items.title: Nathan Lambert — Chinese open models get twice the downloads of US ones
items.summary: Chinese labs now lead open-weight AI on downloads, capability scores, research citations and commercial usage.

items.title: John Berryman — OpenAI could copy Jev, so TypeSafe's moat is its data
items.summary: Jev runs on standard transformer machinery, so John Berryman expects OpenAI to build its own version before long.

items.title: Unreal Agent — an open harness that runs tool calls in the background
items.summary: An MIT-licensed Go harness that keeps the model working while its tools finish.

items.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna — OpenAI's mid and low tiers at half the 5.6 price
items.summary: OpenAI fills in the GPT-6 family below Astra with a balanced tier and a cheap one, both at half the price of their 5.6 predecessors.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.156.0 — an optional fullscreen UI with transcript search
items.summary: A fullscreen terminal UI, searchable transcripts and voice on by default land in Codex CLI 0.156.0.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.280 — Opus 5.5 arrives and Pro plans move off Sonnet
items.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 becomes the default Opus model, and Pro and Team Standard plans now start on Opus instead of Sonnet.

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 — Anthropic's new flagship costs 40% less than Opus 5
items.summary: Anthropic's new top model matches Fable 5.1 on most work while costing 40% less per token than Opus 5.

items.title: Meta's Muse exported 6.8 GB of its own sandbox — including SSH keys
items.summary: An ordinary conversation plus a connected Google Drive pulled 6.8 GB of Muse's own runtime out of its sandbox.

items.title: Hemmingway-1 — a 27B open model tuned for everyday messages
items.summary: A 27B open model that answers a request for an email with the email, and nothing else.

items.title: Colin Breck — AI-drafted proposals cost the reader more than they save the writer
items.summary: The case that generated prose shifts the cost of thinking from the person writing to every person reading.

items.title: Wes Roth — 'AI labs may be hiding their biggest breakthroughs'
items.summary: Wes Roth walks through Scott Aaronson's claim that labs are sitting on maths results they have not published.

items.title: Two Minute Papers — 'Yes, Jev Is Insane, But There's A Catch'
items.summary: Two Minute Papers looks at TypeSafe's Jev, the model that answers with a typed value rather than prose.

items.title: vLLM v0.30.0 — engine restarts skip the disk with a GPU weight cache
items.summary: Fast Start keeps post-quantized weights resident in GPU memory, so a restarting vLLM engine maps them instead of reloading them.

items.title: Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI — nine mathematicians advise OpenAI
items.summary: Nine mathematicians now advise OpenAI on how its AI math results reach the public — with no power to slow the research down.

items.title: Grok 4.7 — xAI's most capable model for coding and knowledge work
items.summary: xAI's Grok 4.7 lifts coding and engineering scores over Grok 4.6 while holding the same $2/$6 price and 500K context.

items.title: MiMo-V2.6 — Xiaomi's trillion-parameter model ships under MIT
items.summary: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6 with open MIT weights, a 1M-token context, and cybersecurity scores far above its own V2.5 line.

items.title: Fireship — 'An ex-OpenAI researcher just deleted language from the LLM...'
items.summary: Fireship walks through Jev, the TypeSafe AI model that answers with a typed decision and a confidence score rather than text.

items.title: Kev — open decision models that answer typed questions in one pass
items.summary: Kev puts the Jev idea — typed questions in, probabilities out — into open Apache-2.0 weights you can train and run yourself.

items.title: mini-AGI — a model that keeps learning on an 8GB laptop GPU
items.summary: mini-AGI trains a byte-level model from scratch on one 8GB laptop GPU and keeps learning without forgetting what it already read.

items.title: Sam Witteveen — 'How to Build Things with Jev & OpenJevs'
items.summary: Sam Witteveen follows his two Jev episodes with a hands-on build using Jev and the open OpenJev checkpoints.

items.title: Pirate Face — open model weights turned into magnet links
items.summary: Pirate Face mirrors open Hugging Face models as checksum-verified torrents, so the weights stay downloadable after the original is pulled.

items.title: Po-Shen Loh — why we still need human mathematicians
items.summary: Po-Shen Loh argues that AI oversight, not faster theorem proving, is what keeps human mathematicians necessary.

items.title: AX v0.3.0 — Google's agent orchestrator moves task state to Redis
items.summary: Google's open agent orchestrator splits into three services and keeps task state in Redis instead of Kubernetes.
